video.title: Fantasy Basketball Mock Draft - Category Pick 12

summary: Josh Lloyd runs a 12-team, 9-category, head-to-head mock draft with a third round reversal from pick 12. He skips the injury-risk players available there (Kawhi, LaMelo, Kyrie, Steph) and takes Austin Reaves, then Karl-Anthony Towns at 13. He says Haliburton, Jalen Johnson, Donovan Mitchell and Scottie Barnes do not belong in the first round, even though Yahoo ranks them there. His main point is that players land 25 to 30 picks apart from one mock to the next with no news in between, so listeners should not copy mock drafts as a blueprint and should adapt during the draft. His final team projects at about a .500 winning percentage and is about even (4.5 to 4.5) against most teams, so he says it will need smart waiver work.

rules.text: At pick 12 he avoids per-game value that comes with injury risk. He prefers a safer player he thinks could finish as a first rounder.
rules.quote: most of my per game projected players in this area are injury risks like Kawawaii even LaMelo, Kyrie, Steph

rules.text: Do not lean too hard on mock drafts. Players move 25 to 30 spots between drafts with no news, so stay flexible and react to what is actually available.
rules.quote: I think there is a real risk in these of it leading you astray. You got to be nimble.

rules.text: Do not copy another drafter's picks. Who is available changes every draft.
rules.quote: don't look at my team and go, "Well, Josh picked at 12. I'm going to take all of his guys."

rules.text: Treat rankings, ADP and past mocks as inputs only. Take what is useful from them, but do not treat them as a clear blueprint.
rules.quote: Take what you need to take out of it, but don't look at it as a clear blueprint.

rules.text: In a third round reversal, the drafter at pick one can still use the fourth pick on an injury-risk star, because three other players are already on the roster.
rules.quote: you can use your fourth pick to take a Kyrie or a Kawawaii at that stage and you've already got three other guys ahead of him

rules.text: Picking on the turn, with two picks in a row, changes your strategy. Use it to target the categories you need, such as assists.
rules.quote: I'm on the turn. I want to get some assists. I'm going to take Dylan Harper.

rules.text: Many drafters ignore 9-category rankings for a lot of players and do not care about perceived value.
rules.quote: nine cat rankings are just really weird because everyone just ignores them for bunches of players

rules.text: Draft upside to win the league. Do not draft safe, low-upside veterans just to make projected standings look good.
rules.quote: are we trying to win a league or a projected standings?

rules.text: Drafting a backup and waiting for an injury ahead of him is harder to make work in a standard format.
rules.quote: that's just an upside play waiting on an injury which is harder to do in a standard format

rules.text: A low-upside player becomes an upside pick if you get him much later than where he projects.
rules.quote: Not really an upside player if you get him 110. But if you get him at 168 that that does become upside.

rules.text: A roster that projects close to even across categories needs smart waiver moves to win.
rules.quote: That means I need smart waiver wiring to get me where I need to go.
